question: Which process completely destroys every single form of microbial life, including tough bacterial spores?
explanation: Sterilization is the powerhouse of infection control! It's the only process that wipes out all microbial life, including stubborn endospores that love to survive ordinary cleaning. [learn more](GST114_U2_T10#GST114_U2_T10_h1)

question: Why do we use gentle antiseptics on human skin instead of strong chemical disinfectants?

options.A: Disinfectants are too expensive for routine skin cleansing
options.B: Antiseptics kill bacterial spores while disinfectants cannot
options.C: Skin tissues require milder chemicals to prevent cellular damage
options.D: Skin oils neutralize the active ingredients in standard disinfectants

explanation: You wouldn't want to pour harsh floor cleaner on a patient's arm! Antiseptics are specially formulated to be gentle and safe for living human tissue without causing burns or damage. [learn more](GST114_U2_T10#GST114_U2_T10_h1)

question: Which level of disinfection kills the tuberculosis bacterium but doesn't necessarily wipe out bacterial spores?
explanation: Think of intermediate-level disinfection as a strong middle ground—it tackles tough bugs like Mycobacterium tuberculosis, even though spores might still hang around. [learn more](GST114_U2_T10#GST114_U2_T10_h2)

question: A flexible camera scope used to check a patient's stomach touches delicate mucous membranes. What level of processing does it need?
explanation: Because semi-critical items like scopes touch mucous membranes, they need high-level disinfection to make sure they are super clean and safe for the next patient. [learn more](GST114_U2_T10#GST114_U2_T10_h2)

question: What is the main catch when using alcohol wipes to clean ward surfaces?

options.A: They leave a sticky chemical residue on all treated surfaces
options.B: They promote the rapid growth of fungal spores on furniture
options.C: They corrode stainless steel surgical instruments within minutes
options.D: They evaporate too quickly to maintain adequate contact time

explanation: Alcohol dries up super fast in the open air! Because it evaporates so quickly, it sometimes doesn't stay wet long enough to kill all the germs on a table or tray. [learn more](GST114_U2_T10#GST114_U2_T10_h3)

question: Which group of chemical disinfectants is notorious for releasing strong, irritating fumes that can make you cough?
explanation: Chemicals like glutaraldehyde (an aldehyde) are great at killing germs, but their vapors are strong! That's why areas using them always need good ventilation. [learn more](GST114_U2_T10#GST114_U2_T10_h3)

question: How does organic matter like blood or stool mess up the disinfection process?

options.A: Accelerating the evaporation rate of the applied solution
options.B: Protecting microorganisms from direct contact with the chemical
options.C: Turning the liquid disinfectant into an inert solid crystal
options.D: Neutralizing the room temperature to below freezing levels

explanation: Blood and dirt act like a tiny shield for germs. If you don't wash them away first, the disinfectant can't actually touch the bacteria underneath to kill them! [learn more](GST114_U2_T10#GST114_U2_T10_h4)

question: Why is thorough washing and cleaning an absolute must before using a high-level disinfectant?

options.A: To ensure the metal instruments do not become magnetized
options.B: To polish the instrument surface so it reflects ultraviolet light
options.C: To reduce the financial cost of purchasing liquid chemicals
options.D: To remove soil and protein loads that neutralize antimicrobial activity

explanation: Remember: you can't properly disinfect a dirty surface! Washing removes protein and dirt that would otherwise block or weaken your disinfectant. [learn more](GST114_U2_T10#GST114_U2_T10_h4)

question: What level of processing is required for a medical device classified as semi-critical?
explanation: Semi-critical devices touch mucous membranes, so they need high-level disinfection to knock out almost all microorganisms (minus a few tough spores). [learn more](GST114_U2_T10#GST114_U2_T10_h5)

question: You are getting a blood pressure cuff ready for the next patient in the ward. How should this non-critical item be cleaned?
explanation: Since a BP cuff only touches intact skin, it is a non-critical item. A simple low-level disinfection wipe-down between patients is all it needs! [learn more](GST114_U2_T10#GST114_U2_T10_h5)

question: When cleaning a ward room, why should your wiping motions start from high surfaces and move down toward the floor?

options.A: Debris and dust naturally fall downward during the wiping action
options.B: Chemical disinfectants lose weight when applied to upper shelves
options.C: Floor bacteria jump upward onto clean furniture if done incorrectly
options.D: Bending over to clean lower areas first causes severe back strain

explanation: It's all about gravity! Dust and crumbs naturally fall down as you wipe. If you clean top-to-bottom, you'll sweep up all that debris when you finally mop the floor. [learn more](GST114_U2_T10#GST114_U2_T10_h6)

question: When wiping down a patient's bed rail, what technique is most important for actually getting rid of germs?

options.A: Using a dry cotton duster to absorb liquid residue
options.B: Waiting thirty seconds before touching the damp surface
options.C: Applying physical friction with the wipe to remove biofilm
options.D: Pouring neat bleach directly onto the rail without wiping

explanation: Elbow grease matters! Rubbing with a cloth provides physical friction that breaks up stubborn germ films that chemicals alone might leave behind. [learn more](GST114_U2_T10#GST114_U2_T10_h6)

question: What protective gear is a must-have when you are mixing and diluting strong, concentrated liquid disinfectants?

options.A: Heavy-duty utility gloves and eye protection
options.B: Disposable cloth theatre boots and masks
options.D: Sterile surgical gloves and paper caps

explanation: Concentrated chemicals can splash and cause nasty burns to your eyes or skin. Always protect yourself with heavy-duty gloves and eye protection! [learn more](GST114_U2_T10#GST114_U2_T10_h7)

question: When mixing chemical disinfectants, why must you always pour the concentrated chemical into water, rather than water into the chemical?

options.A: To stop the chemical container from dissolving in the sink
options.B: To prevent dangerous splashing and exothermic chemical reactions
options.C: To ensure the water temperature stays at freezing point
options.D: To prevent the mixture from turning into a thick gel

explanation: Safety first! Adding water to a strong chemical can cause a violent, hot splash (an exothermic reaction) that could burn you. Always add chemical to water! [learn more](GST114_U2_T10#GST114_U2_T10_h7)
